title: Field Research & Model Gap Radar: Continuous Competitive Tracking Playbook
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Goal:
Create a repeatable playbook that marries field research, telemetry signals, and competitive intelligence to surface model capability gaps, prioritize integration work, and inform go/no-go decisions for onboarding new open models or model variants.

Background:
We frequently see feature requests and partner asks that depend on niche model capabilities (e.g., long-context coherence, structured JSON fidelity, instruction-following for domain-specific tokens). Existing landscape trackers are snapshot-based and miss drift and subtle regressions. This playbook defines a continuous process and rubric for discovering, scoring, and escalating model gaps into product and engineering work.

Scope (what this ticket delivers):
- Documented end-to-end playbook for field research and model gap radar (README + step checklist).
- Signal catalogue: prioritized list of telemetry, external signals, and qualitative inputs to monitor.
- Scoring rubric to convert signals into a triage score (impact x frequency x integration cost).
- Template artifacts: intake form for field reports, standard evaluation probe scaffold, and stakeholder notification templates.
- Rollout plan to pilot the playbook with two product teams (Console and API).

Primary audiences:
- Product managers (prioritization & roadmaps)
- Model ops & SRE (integration cost & feasibility)
- Developer relations & solutions (field signals)

Signal sources (examples):
- Customer support tickets mentioning 'hallucination', 'stability', or 'formatting' (weekly agg).
- Console cost/latency regressions when switching models (per-release delta).
- A/B evaluation harness failures for internal evals (drop in QA score > 3 pts).
- Public model release notes and community threads (monthly sweep).
- Partner integrations and field demos (ad hoc reports).

Scoring rubric (simplified):
- Impact (3 = user-facing correctness; 2 = degraded UX; 1 = edge case)
- Frequency (3 = widespread across customers; 2 = multiple customers or repeated; 1 = isolated)
- Integration Cost (3 = low cost to patch; 2 = moderate engineering work; 1 = high dependency/project)
Triage score = Impact * Frequency * Integration Cost (range 1-27).

Priority buckets (example):
- 20-27 -> High: schedule into next sprint cycle and assign ENG follow up.
- 10-19 -> Medium: add to backlog with PM-written spec and measurement plan.
- 1-9 -> Low: monitor and re-evaluate after 1 month.

Operational workflow:
1. Intake: Field reports submitted via the form (links below) and auto-tagged into the Model Radar board.
2. Enrichment: PMs attach telemetry (error rates, latency, eval diffs) and assign preliminary scores.
3. Triage meeting (weekly, 30m): Review new entries, validate signals, and assign to priority buckets.
4. Investigation sprint: For High items, kick off a 1-2 week discovery with Eng/Research to validate root cause and remediation approach.
5. Decision: Recommend action (model switch, prompt engineering, runtime optimization, or schedule feature work).
6. Closure & retrospective: Capture outcome, attach PR/Playbook updates, and adjust scoring if necessary.

Deliverables & artifacts:
- Playbook doc (Confluence): Field Research & Model Gap Radar (link placeholder).
- Intake form (Google Form / internal tool).
- Evaluation probe scaffold (GitHub repo with tests).
- Weekly Model Radar board (Linear view).
- Pilot summary for Console and API teams (slide deck).

Acceptance criteria:
- Playbook doc reviewed and approved by PM, Eng lead, and Research (sign-offs captured).
- Signal catalogue populated with at least 12 signals across telemetry, field, and public sources.
- Scoring rubric applied to 6 historical incidents and triage results documented.
- Two pilot teams have intake flows enabled and submitted at least one real report each.
- Rollout plan with training session scheduled.

Success metrics (90 days post-rollout):
- Median time from field report -> triage decision reduced to <= 7 days.
- >=50% of high-triage gaps have an engineering action (PR, rollback, or model pin) within 30 days.
- Product teams report increased confidence (survey NPS-style) in model selection decisions (+15 points).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Signal noise leads to unnecessary churn.
  Mitigation: Require telemetry-backed validation for High prioritization; use historic baselining.
- Risk: Overlap with existing incident workflows.
  Mitigation: Integrate with incident tooling and define clear boundaries (this playbook covers non-SEV model capability gaps).

Next steps (this ticket):
- Draft initial playbook doc and signal catalogue (owner: Liam).
- Build intake form and add to the Model Radar board (owner: Ops PM).
- Run two-week pilot with Console and API product teams.
- Present pilot findings to Product Council and Research.
